critique: MERGE: PASS — The script correctly uses MERGE INTO for all Delta loads (dimensions and fact). No mode("overwrite") found.

Hardcoding: FAIL — Multiple hardcoded values exist: (a) the src table mapping dictionary (e.g., "Production.Products", "Sales.Orders"); (b) default layer prefixes and TARGET_SCHEMA defaults (e.g., "gold", "dim_") are embedded as string literals rather than fully required context parameters. The audit rule requires zero hardcoded paths/identifiers; these must come from the provided context/param store.

Unknown member handling (Lookups): PARTIAL — The fact-product lookup uses COALESCE to map missing product SKs to UNKNOWN_SURROGATE which satisfies the 'unknown member' requirement for product -> dim_product. However, other lookups (if present) must also use explicit COALESCE/unknown surrogate logic. Also the change-detection logic uses COALESCE(..., '') for all attribute columns which is unsafe for non-string types and can yield incorrect change detection for numeric/decimal/timestamp fields.

Casting precision: WARNING/FAIL — The script enforces casts with an assumed schema (e.g., DecimalType(18,2) for unit_price/discount). The pipeline must use the exact target DDL precision/scale (from the provided Solution DDLs). The script currently uses 'assumed' schemas rather than consuming the authoritative DDL; this risks precision loss. This is a hard compliance fail until target DDLs are applied precisely.

Resiliency & Logging: FAIL — The job emits high-level logger.info messages around MERGE steps, but does not log row counts or diagnostics (e.g., staging row counts, number of rows expired, inserted, updated, deleted) before/after each MERGE. There is no per-table error-state handling (e.g., capturing and logging row-level errors, count of null surrogate assignments). The exception block logs the stack trace, but does not surface per-step metrics required for operational observability.

SCD2 change detection: FLAW — build_attr_change_condition performs COALESCE(column, '') comparisons for every attr column. This is type-unsafe: numeric/decimal/timestamp columns should use COALESCE(..., <type-appropriate-default>) or use NULL-safe SQL operators (IS DISTINCT FROM where supported) or explicit casts to canonical textual representation. Current expression may mis-detect changes (e.g., NULL vs 0 for numeric).

Parameterization / Contract: FAIL — enforce_casts uses in-script assumed schema maps. The code must obtain the exact target DDL (column names, types, precisions/scales) from a canonical metadata service or be injected in 'context' so that casts match target definitions exactly. Also, target table names are derived from prefix defaults — these must be required context parameters, not fallbacks.
Medallion structure: PASS — The code shows clear Extract, Transform, Load sections and SCD2 pattern for dimensions which aligns with medallion-style pipeline structure.

SQL MERGE correctness: NOTE — The SCD2 merge patterns are two-step and generally correct; however the 'expire' MERGE uses ON tgt.business_key = src.business_key AND tgt.is_current = true and WHEN MATCHED AND (change_expr) THEN UPDATE SET ... This will not detect changes where the business_key didn't match (i.e., business key changes) — ensure business key semantics are validated. Also the insert MERGE uses src.start_date directly — confirm src.start_date is deterministic and corresponds to intended event timestamp.

Other technical concerns: (a) enforce_casts uses DataType instances when calling cast(); confirm runtime accepts DataType objects (some runtimes expect string type names); (b) the script assumes target dimensional tables will auto-generate SKs — if SK assignment is not guaranteed by the target, explicit SK generation logic is required for idempotency and referential joins.
